notes: The V4.1 cache now accepts registered Q2_K/Q4_K R4 experts. GPU kernels preserve the block-32 FP8 activation boundary followed by GGML Q8_K encoding, route weighting before down-input quantization, clipping, BF16 projection boundaries, and ordered per-expert reduction. It borrows existing pinned NUMA weights with zero host weight snapshot.

One model load uses equal serial layer placement on two GPUs. An initial 12 GiB per GPU attempt failed with CUDA out of memory on long prefill, so the full benchmark uses a fixed 8 GiB budget per GPU. Startup warmup allocates these caches before Python controls; the controls disable dispatch while retaining the payload. Controls set_moe_cuda_cache(0) to disable dispatch; retained cache records stay allocated during formal controls.

Off-cache warmups generate 64 short ordinary tokens, 64 short DSpark tokens and the long retrieval response. Then cache warmups generate 256 short ordinary tokens, 256 short DSpark tokens and the long retrieval response. Three alternating formal short requests per mode, arithmetic/code fixtures, three alternating long DSpark requests per mode and one long ordinary control per mode follow.

Cache counters synchronize CUDA outside request timing. The V4.1 route trace is enabled at its built-in reporting intervals. Lookup counters do not represent all NUMA routes; route traces report actual CPU/GPU splits.

CUDA cache retains live residency and adaptive scheduling across requests. Numerical differences can change generated text, draft acceptance and route selection; compare paired outputs and acceptance before attributing throughput changes solely to compute acceleration.
Timing is native launch to first token and then first-to-last token throughput; excludes loading, tokenization and HTTP. Prefix/history caching is disabled. Fast prefill is enabled.
The long retrieval task only generates about 30 tokens. Functional fixtures and these timing results do not establish complete model accuracy or general conversation performance.

The historical single-GPU reference uses the same installed library and CPU/model settings, with 0 or 3 GiB GPU expert records. Its requests were measured in a separate process; use the in-process dual-GPU controls to isolate cache effects, and inspect output/acceptance differences before comparing throughput.
